item.title: Incarico post-doc: IpD52/2026:"Study of the Influence of Soil, Climatic, and Technological Factors on the Variability and Characterization of the Sensory Space of Lugana Wine " (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-07 Scienze e tecnologie alimentari

The research program aims to characterize the sensory space of Lugana wines through two complementary approaches: Quantitative Descriptive Analysis (QDA) and fast profiling (FP) techniques. QDA, conducted by a trained panel, will enable the identification and quantification of the wines’ olfactory, gustatory, and visual attributes. FP methods will be used to explore sensory similarities and differences among samples, identifying groups of wines and their characteristic descriptors. Integrating these two approaches will make it possible to define and compare the sensory spaces of wines from different areas, highlighting their distinctive characteristics and variability. item.title: Incarico post-doc: IpD51/2026:"Physiological and agronomic characterization of TEA grapevine prototypes genetically improved for tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses." (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-03 Scienze e tecnologie dei sistemi arborei e forestali

The research program focuses on the phenotyping of gene-edited grapevine plants during the field-testing phase. The vines to be characterized are TEA plants edited for genes associated with susceptibility to downy and powdery mildew, as well as for metabolic pathways involved in grape quality. Activities will entail agronomic characterization and the monitoring of physiological parameters to evaluate plant performance in the cultivation environment, in relation to genotype and in response to potential abiotic stresses (e.g., water deficit).

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Interactions between innovative cover crops, grain legumes, and weeds – the role of allelopathy. (Sc.Sup. S.Anna PISA)
item.description:

Institution: Sc.Sup. S.Anna PISA, Pisa
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-02 Agronomia e sistemi colturali erbacei e ortofloricoli

The candidate will determine the allelopathic potential of innovative cover crops belonging to the Brassicaceae and Fabaceae families by assessing their effects on the germination and growth of target species. He/She will also be responsible for identifying and characterizing the bioactive compounds released by these cover crops. Furthermore, the candidate will actively participate in the chickpea Living Lab activities coordinated by Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna, working with Living Lab members to evaluate whether and how innovative cover crops can be incorporated into crop rotations to optimize weed management in subsequent chickpea crops.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Definition of innovative agronomic protocols for the productive and qualitative enhancement of durum wheat in Southern Italy (Univ. PALERMO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-05 23:59
Institution: Univ. PALERMO, Palermo
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-02 Agronomia e sistemi colturali erbacei e ortofloricoli

The project involves the development and validation of innovative agronomic protocols for the valorization of durum wheat. The strategies adopted will include the use of new generation biostimulants (both microbial and non-microbial), with the aim of reducing chemical inputs and promoting environmental sustainability. The effectiveness of these approaches will be evaluated in the field through the monitoring of the physiological and production parameters of the crop. Finally, the environmental impact of the proposed methods will be quantified through the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology

item.description:

Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-08 Microbiologia agraria, alimentare e ambientale

The research activity will focus on microbial populations associated with food and agro-environmental matrices using culture-dependent and -independent approaches. Main microbial groups will be quantified using conventional microbiological techniques and selective and/or differential media. Microorganisms of interest will be isolated, purified, identified, and preserved for phenotypic and functional characterization. DNA extracted directly from the matrices will be used for metataxonomic analyses targeting the 16S rRNA and ITS/26S rRNA genes. Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-06 Genetica, chimica e pedologia agraria e forestale

The research programme aims to investigate and valorise the genetic and functional diversity of alpha-amylase/trypsin inhibitors (ATIs) in wheat to develop healthier and more sustainable varieties and food products. The activities will include the genomic characterisation of a broad panel of *Triticum* genotypes through targeted long-read sequencing, analysis of variation at ATI loci, and integration of genomic data with information on ATI content and immunostimulatory potential. Low-ATI wheat lines will be selected and evaluated, and strategies will be developed to valorise milling by-products, such as bran and germ, through controlled fermentation with lactic acid bacteria. The research project focuses on carbon, water, and energy fluxes between the soil–plant system and the atmosphere in apple orchards. Activities will include collecting meteorological and flux data using an eddy covariance station, assessing data quality for processing, generating indicators such as NEP, GPP, NECB, and ET, and developing predictive models in the context of climate change.
